B01.evidence: The full typed words par l’Inspection Académique were inspected. The isolated block above a has no two sloping arms of a circumflex; an analogous detached irregular dot occurs above c. Both differ from the complete slanting acute over é. These copy marks do not securely establish an extra accent. Retain Académique, with the rejected accent hypothesis documented here rather than treating a print blemish as a new letter.

The independent lower line exposes only upper bowls and strokes. Retain both illegible units, and do not complete the second from the sender name.

B04.evidence: The closer view shows two top bowls, paired upright tips and paired sloping tips. No R leg, U base or X crossing survives below the black image edge. Although these tops permit the conjecture ROUX, they cannot establish those complete letters. Physical clipping, not a recovered name, is recorded.
